value.title: HackerOne Disclosed Top SQLi: Header-Based & Second-Order Injection Vectors
value.content: {"id": "intel_hackerone_top_sqli", "topic": "sqli", "title": "HackerOne Disclosed Top SQLi: Header-Based & Second-Order Injection Vectors", "source_url": "https://github.com/reddelexc/hackerone-reports/blob/master/docs/tops_by_bug_type/TOPSQLI.md", "prerequisites": ["http_headers", "sql_concatenation", "second_order_execution"], "signals": ["x_forwarded_for", "user_agent_logging", "client_ip_header", "json_extract_operator", "second_order_deferred_execution"], "verification_strategy": "Probe non-standard HTTP request headers (X-Forwarded-For, Client-IP, User-Agent) utilized in audit logging scripts with non-destructive boolean expressions or sleep probes. For second-order vectors, submit stored profile data and monitor subsequent administrative reporting endpoints.", "evidence_requirements": ["header_dependent_differential", "audit_log_sql_syntax_error", "deferred_execution_divergence"], "remediation": "Treat all HTTP request headers as untrusted user input. Bind client IP, User-Agent, and session telemetry using parameterized queries before inserting into security audit logs.", "description": "Analysis of high-bounty HackerOne disclosed reports reveals that SQLi frequently exists outside ordinary GET/POST query parameters. Common enterprise vectors include background analytics logging headers, JSON operators in PostgreSQL (->>) or MySQL (JSON_EXTRACT) concatenated without sanitization, and second-order injections where data stored during registration triggers an injection when batch administrative jobs run."}
